html:
The arrival of Buddhism in Japan from Korea in the 6th century. The Nihon Shoki chronicle says that in 552 King Seong of Baekje sent the Japanese court a bronze Buddha and sutras; other sources give 538. Both dates are traditional, and immigrant families likely practised the faith earlier.

The gift split the court of Yamato Japan. The Soga clan backed the new religion; the Mononobe and Nakatomi clans held to the native gods and blamed an epidemic on it. The Soga won by force in 587. Prince Shōtoku then promoted Buddhism, built temples such as Hōryū-ji and wrote it into his Seventeen-article constitution.

Buddhism brought with it Chinese writing, building, art and ideas of the state. It came to sit beside, and mix with, the worship of the kami that later became known as Shinto. Japan's great Buddhist temples, and later schools such as Pure Land and Zen, grew from this start.
